features.method: Published coordinate (29d21'27.56"N, 100d08'19.66"E) from the LHAASO Collaboration's own Chinese Physics C paper (doi:10.1088/1674-1137/ac3fa6), converted from DMS to decimal degrees. Supersedes the prior OSM/Nominatim rest-area geocode reused verbatim from site:lhaaso-haizi-mountain (precision_m 5000): that point sat 3253 m away, inside its own claimed accuracy but far coarser than this published figure. The previously-attempted LHAASO Science Book source (arXiv:1905.02773) remains unfetchable by any means tried across two research sessions (WebFetch, ar5iv, arxiv.org/html, r.jina.ai) -- this independent Chinese Physics C paper was found and fetched instead. KM2A is independently sourced as circular (radius ~575 m core, ~635 m outer guard ring) and WCDA as 78,000 m2 (two 150x150 m pools plus one 300x110 m pool); drawing them is now unblocked by this tighter anchor (50 m, well under either shape's own size) but is left as backlog for a future pass, since it requires deciding each shape's own orientation/offset from this point, which no source fetched in this review states.

provenance.locator: Chinese Physics C 46, 030001 (2022), Chapter 1 'LHAASO Instruments and Detector technology', DOI 10.1088/1674-1137/ac3fa6
provenance.note: QA pass (2026-09-21): replaced the previous OSM/Nominatim rest-area geocode (precision_m 5000) with this peer-reviewed, collaboration-authored published coordinate, independently fetched and confirmed verbatim on two separate mirrors (iopscience.iop.org and cpc.ihep.ac.cn) during this review -- see docs/atlas-worklog/REVIEW_geometry_qa.md. Haversine distance from the old point: 3253 m, inside the old record's own claimed 5000 m accuracy_m, so the previous point was not dishonest, just far coarser than necessary now that a survey-grade figure is available. representation upgraded georeferenced -> surveyed and confidence approximate -> verified (rank-10 journal_article source, per contract SS1.2). accuracy_m tightened 5000 -> 50: the quoted arc-second figure implies sub-metre nominal precision, but 50 m is kept as an honest allowance since the quote describes the observatory's general Mt. Haizi location, not a specific surveyed structure corner.
provenance.quote: The Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO) (Fig. 1) is located at Mt. Haizi (4410 m a.s.l., 600 g/cm2, 29°21'27.56"N, 100°08'19.66"E) in Daocheng, Sichuan province, P.R. China.

summary.plain: The LHAASO cosmic-ray and gamma-ray observatory on Haizi Mountain, Daocheng County, Sichuan, China.
